correctness.rationale: The chosen one-parameter subgroup has pairwise distinct weights on all matrix coordinates. Every defining permanent is a semi-invariant because each monomial has the same row-plus-column weight. At a coordinate point only one matrix entry is nonzero, while every permanent with r at least two is a sum of monomials using r distinct row-column positions, so every permanent vanishes. Thus the fixed locus is exactly the mn coordinate points. Euler localization applies to arbitrary complex algebraic varieties, including singular or reducible ones, and projectivity identifies compactly supported and ordinary Euler characteristic. The complement statement follows by constructible additivity. The bundled checker independently verifies weight separation, semi-invariance, and coordinate-point vanishing on a finite regression grid.

value.rationale: Permanental varieties are natural counterparts of determinantal rank varieties and are explicitly described in recent literature as geometrically poorly understood. The theorem computes a canonical global topological invariant uniformly for every matrix size and every permanental rank threshold, including the permanent hypersurface central to geometric complexity theory. The answer is structurally rigid: all nonlinear permanental equations are invisible to ordinary Euler characteristic, and the complement always has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. This is a natural all-family topological collapse, not a small numerical slice or a recomputation of a known table.
